stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria with no existing spec; cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview is complex and needs elaboration first, then hardening for testability, security, and edge cases.

agentContributions.notes: Live Preview is a novel capability. The attachment point is useContent (236+ callers) — the single hook every component uses to fetch content via getContentByKey. Live preview must integrate there so draft/unpublished content from Contentstack's preview mechanism flows through the same interface without changing downstream consumers. VCs derived solely from description since ACs are empty.

Openspec provided empty acceptanceCriteria, so all ACs are derived from the story title, technical file references, and openspec's note about useContent/getContentByKey integration. Without access to file contents, I inferred that Contentstack Live Preview uses a preview token/session mechanism (industry-standard for Contentstack) and that the ContentstackContext provides the SDK client. Key design decisions reflected in ACs: (1) AC-7 enforces the 'no downstream consumer changes' constraint from openspec's note; (2) AC-8 addresses security — draft content must never leak to non-preview users; (3) AC-5 covers graceful degradation on API failure; (4) AC-11 covers ContentstackLink specifically since it's listed as a key file and handles references; (5) AC-13 addresses deep resolution of nested content which is a common gap in CMS preview implementations; (6) AC-12 covers session lifecycle. I could not verify actual ContentstackContext API shape or preview token mechanism without reading the files — if the actual implementation uses a fundamentally different activation pattern, AC-3 and AC-9 may need adjustment.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: All four manifest paths verified as EXISTS — no missing files. Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the architectural integration point (useContent hook with 236+ callers) and the critical no-downstream-change constraint; speckit derived verification criteria covering security (draft leakage prevention), graceful degradation, session lifecycle, nested content resolution, and ContentstackLink-specific handling. The collaboration is well-structured. However, speckit explicitly states it could not verify the actual ContentstackContext API shape or preview token mechanism — AC-3 and AC-9 are predicated on assumptions about Contentstack's preview activation pattern that may not match the real implementation. Since all criteria were derived from the title and file references alone (no original ACs to anchor against), and the story covers a complex cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview capability, a human should confirm that the inferred API integration points match the actual ContentstackContext and useContent implementations before implementation begins.
